issues.description: Entire compiled script is sent over RPC for every compile, inflating payload size
issues.detail: compile_notebook now reads the full script_content and returns it in the RPC response, even when the user never clicks Download. For large pipelines this duplicates the file in memory and across the wire. Consider a lazy endpoint (GET script by path) invoked only on click.

issues.description: No encoding specified when reading script; may fail on non-ASCII content
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding. Generated pipelines can contain user docstrings/comments with unicode. On Windows or systems with non-UTF-8 locales this can raise UnicodeDecodeError and fail compilation. Use open(script_path, encoding='utf-8').

issues.description: Download icon lacks accessible button semantics and keyboard support
issues.detail: GetAppIcon is rendered as an SVG with onClick but no role, tabIndex, or keyboard handler. Screen reader and keyboard users cannot trigger the download. Wrap in a <button> or IconButton with aria-label, matching the sibling <a> link's affordances.

issues.description: Download icon appears even when compiledContent is missing, producing a silent no-op
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick guards on props.compiledContent but the icon is always rendered in the success branch. If content is absent (older backend, error during read), clicking does nothing with no feedback. Either hide the icon or show a tooltip/disabled state.

issues.description: Fallback filename 'pipeline.kale.py' hides bug if compiledPath is empty
issues.detail: split('/').pop() on an empty string yields '' which falls back to the default name. That's fine, but the real risk is Windows-style paths or trailing slashes producing odd names. Consider using path.basename equivalent and validating compiledPath is non-empty before enabling download.

issues.description: Compiled script content kept in React state for the session may retain sensitive data
issues.detail: compiledContent persists in DeployProgressState until the panel is dismissed. Pipelines can embed credentials/secrets passed via metadata. There's no explicit cleanup after download or on unmount beyond component teardown. Consider clearing after use or documenting retention.

review.summary: The feature works but ships the entire compiled script through the RPC response on every compile, which is wasteful and could be replaced by a lazy fetch on click. The backend file read also lacks an explicit utf-8 encoding, risking failures on non-ASCII content. On the UI side, the new download affordance is a bare SVG with onClick — no button semantics, aria-label, or keyboard handler — and silently no-ops when content is missing. Minor concerns around filename handling and retention of script content in state.
